topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the hallmarks of cancer framework, outlining learning outcomes, and reviewing prior concepts of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Sustained Proliferative Signaling and Evasion of Growth Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream signaling cascades, such as Wnt/beta-catenin and RTK/Ras/PI3K pathways, drive autonomous proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells exhibit a differentiation block across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelial carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through genetic alterations affecting p53, Bax, and Bcl-2 signaling.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescent Stress Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells achieve replicative immortality by maintaining telomeres and overcoming p53-mediated senescence stress responses.

topics.label: Altered Cancer Metabolism and Complex Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex physiological hallmarks and detail how cancer cells reprogram their metabolism through aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the requirement for tumor vascularization, its onset during neoplastic progression, and the balance of angiogenic activators and inhibitors.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Bottlenecks of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes the multi-step metastatic cascade, diagnostic detection of disseminated cells, and the genomic features underlying metastatic capability.

topics.label: Conclusion and Final Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with closing reflections on the evolution of cancer hallmarks, recommended literature, and session wrap-up.
